name: Shatabhisha
description: A star 118 parsecs away, 98 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112961: radius 98.304 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 1630.73 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.103) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112961: effective temperature 3702 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.181)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112961: distance 118.064 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.078), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 118 parsecs away, 98 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 1,631 times the Sun's luminosity at 3,702 K, so 98.304 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 112961: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Lambda Aquarii
quotes.card: Lambda Aquarii, Latinized from λ Aquarii and formally named Shatabhisha, is a variable star in the equatorial constellation of Aquarius.
quotes.introduction: The apparent visual magnitude of this star ranges from 3.57 down to 3.80, which is bright enough to be visible with the naked eye.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 2610370969483589888 (quality A), from 2009A&A...498..627F; Gaia DR3 measures none
